# File System (fs)

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Node-`fs`-shaped synchronous file I/O for reading/writing config, data, and logs — not `File`/`FileReader`/`FileSystemFileHandle` (those model browser sandbox/permission concepts that don't exist for a native CLI/microservice program with direct filesystem access).

**Coverage**: 21/22 (~95%) · **Strict Coverage**: 5/22 (~23%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fs.readFileSync(path[, 'utf8'])` | ✅ | • With an encoding the string is strlen-based: a file with an embedded null byte reads back truncated there (the Buffer form keeps every byte) ([ADR-00785](../adr/ADR-00785.md)) | • With no encoding the result is a `Buffer` of the file's exact bytes, as in Node; with an encoding (a bare string or `{ encoding }`: utf8, hex, base64, base64url, latin1, ascii, utf16le) it is the bytes decoded as `buf.toString(encoding)` ([ADR-00785](../adr/ADR-00785.md), [ADR-01163](../adr/ADR-01163.md))<br>• A file descriptor in place of the path reads it to its end: `readFileSync(0)` is stdin<br>• Throws a catchable `Error` (built from `strerror(errno)`) if the file can't be opened; its `.message` is byte-exact to Node's `ENOENT: …, open '<path>'` form, and `err.code`/`syscall`/`path`/`errno` all match ([ADR-00768](../adr/ADR-00768.md), [ADR-01000](../adr/ADR-01000.md))<br>• Pseudo-files under `/proc` and `/sys` (which report `st_size` 0 yet stream real bytes) read correctly — the read grows to EOF rather than trusting the stat size ([ADR-00811](../adr/ADR-00811.md))<br>• See [ADR-00023](../adr/ADR-00023.md), [ADR-00094](../adr/ADR-00094.md) |
| `fs.writeFileSync(path, data[, opts])` | ✅ | • The options argument supports only `{ encoding: 'utf8', flag, mode }` — a non-`'utf8'` encoding is a clean rejection ([ADR-00785](../adr/ADR-00785.md), [ADR-00988](../adr/ADR-00988.md)).<br>• A file descriptor in place of the path (`fs.writeFileSync(fd, …)`) is a compile error | • Creates or truncates the file with `data`. Throws on failure<br>• `data` may be a string (the `strlen`-based path) or a Buffer/TypedArray (binary-safe, writes the real byte count via `fwrite` directly — [ADR-00094](../adr/ADR-00094.md)), dispatched on `data`'s inferred type; a bare `ArrayBuffer` throws Node's `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` `TypeError`<br>• Optional third argument: `'utf8'` (or `{ encoding: 'utf8', flag, mode }`); `{ flag: 'a' }` appends instead of truncating, `{ flag: 'w' }` (default) truncates ([ADR-00785](../adr/ADR-00785.md))<br>• `{ mode }` sets the permission bits when the write creates the file — applied only on creation and reduced by the umask, matching Node/`open(2)` (ignored for a file that already exists) ([ADR-00988](../adr/ADR-00988.md)) |
| `fs.appendFileSync(path, data[, opts])` | ✅ | • The options argument supports only `{ encoding: 'utf8', flag, mode }` — a non-`'utf8'` encoding is a clean rejection ([ADR-00785](../adr/ADR-00785.md), [ADR-00988](../adr/ADR-00988.md)).<br>• A file descriptor in place of the path (`fs.appendFileSync(fd, …)`) is a compile error | • Like `writeFileSync`, but appends instead of truncating (creates the file if it doesn't exist). Throws on failure<br>• Same string/Buffer/TypedArray dispatch as `writeFileSync` (a bare `ArrayBuffer` throws)<br>• Optional third argument `'utf8'` / `{ encoding: 'utf8', flag, mode }` accepted (the flag is a no-op — it always appends); `{ mode }` sets the permission bits when the append creates the file (umask-reduced, only on creation — [ADR-00988](../adr/ADR-00988.md)) ([ADR-00785](../adr/ADR-00785.md)) |
| `fs.existsSync(path)` | ✅ | | • Plain existence check via POSIX `access()`<br>• Deliberately does **not** throw for a missing path — matches real Node's own `existsSync`, one of the few `fs` functions that reports "doesn't exist" as `false` rather than an error |

| `File` / `FileReader` / `FileSystemFileHandle` (browser-flavored File API) | ❌ | | **Differentiator (scoped — [TDD-00172](../tdd/TDD-00172.md)).** Splits in two: the **data layer** (`File extends Blob`, `FileReader.readAsText`/`ArrayBuffer`/`DataURL`) is a thin fs-backed reinterpretation with no UI — path-backed `File`s, reads firing `onload` on the event loop; the **picker layer** (`showOpenFilePicker` → `FileSystemFileHandle`) resolves a path through a pluggable UI backend — a `klain:tui` file-picker widget, a `klain:webview` native dialog, or an explicit-path degradation when headless. Serves interactive native apps (TUI file managers/editors); the data layer is the near-term, standalone-useful piece. |
